title: Weil conjectures for a smooth proper variety
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth, proper, geometrically connected scheme of pure
dimension $d$ over $\Fq$. Put $X=X_0\times_{\Fq}k$, let
$\mathscr X$ be the resulting smooth-proper datum, and let
$P_i=P_i(\mathscr X)$ be the canonical factors of
Definition *Canonical integral cohomological factors*. Then the following
statements hold.

1. The zeta series has both point-counting descriptions
$$
Z(X_0,T)=
\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}
\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})\frac{T^n}{n}\right)
=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}(1-T^{\deg(x)})^{-1},
$$
and belongs to $1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]\cap\mathbf Q(T)$.
1. The polynomials $P_i$ are the unique polynomials
$$
P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]
\qquad(0\leq i\leq2d)
$$
with $P_i(0)=1$ such that, for every prime $\ell\neq p$,
$$
\bigl((\mathbf Z[T]\longrightarrow\Ql[T])(P_i)\bigr)(T)=
\det(1-TF\mid H^i(X,\Ql)).
$$
They give the rational factorization
$$
Z(X_0,T)=
\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}.
$$
1. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$
and regard $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$ inside
$\overline{\mathbf Q}[T]$. For every $0\leq i\leq2d$, every
reciprocal root $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $P_i$ is an
algebraic integer
and a $q$-Weil number of weight $i$:
$$
|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}
$$
for every embedding
$\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$. For every ordinary
root $\beta\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $P_i$ and every embedding
$\tau:\mathbf Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$, one has
$|\tau(\beta)|=q^{-i/2}$.
1. For every $0\leq i\leq2d$, with $b_i=\deg P_i$, and every
prime $\ell\neq p$,
$$
b_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql),
\qquad b_i=b_{2d-i},
\qquad b_0=b_{2d}=1,
$$
independently of $\ell$. Moreover
$$
P_0(T)=1-T,
\qquad
P_{2d}(T)=1-q^dT.
$$
In particular $Z(X_0,T)$ has a pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=1$
and, if $d\geq1$, a pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=q^{-d}$.
1. If
$$
D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T),
\qquad
\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i,
$$
then $d\chi$ is even and, for every $0\leq i\leq2d$,
$$
P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})
=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T),
$$
and
$$
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})
=\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}T^\chi Z(X_0,T)
$$
for the sign
$$
\varepsilon=
(-1)^\chi q^{-d\chi/2}
\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}
\in\{1,-1\}.
$$

proof.text:
*The datum and the factors.* Over the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0=\Fq,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], the hypotheses on $X_0$ are those of [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses] (smooth of pure dimension $d$, proper, geometrically connected), so $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ with $X=X_0	imes_{\Fq}k$ is a smooth-proper datum in the sense of [def-weil-smooth-proper-datum]. For every prime $\ell
eq p$ the smooth-proper cohomological family $(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ of [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family] is therefore defined, with $V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql)$, $F_{i,\ell}$ the geometric Frobenius $F$ restricted to it, and $P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})$; this determinant is what the statement writes $\det(1-TF\mid H^i(X,\Ql))$ (the blueprint's 'Frobenius characteristic factors' are these $P_{i,\ell}$). By [def-weil-canonical-integral-factors], the canonical factors $P_i=P_i(\mathscr X)$, $0\leq i\leq2d$, are the members of the unique tuple in $\mathbf Z[T]^{2d+1}$ with $P_i(0)=1$ and $(\mathbf Z[T]	o\Ql[T])(P_i)=P_{i,\ell}$ for every prime $\ell
eq p$. Theorem [thm-weil-final-integrality], applied to the same $X_0$, asserts that for each $i$ there is exactly one polynomial in $\mathbf Z[T]$ with constant term $1$ whose coefficientwise extension equals $\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\Ql))=P_{i,\ell}$ for every $\ell
eq p$, and calls it the integral Frobenius factor of degree $i$. The canonical factor $P_i(\mathscr X)$ has exactly this property, so by that uniqueness it is the integral Frobenius factor of degree $i$ of [thm-weil-final-integrality]. Theorems III, IV and V below are stated for 'the integral Frobenius factors provided by [thm-weil-final-integrality]', hence for these same $P_i$; so every clause below concerns the same $X_0$, $X$, $Z(X_0,T)$ and $P_i$ as the five theorems I--V.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph ('The hypotheses make $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ a smooth-proper datum ...'); the identification of the canonical factors with the integral Frobenius factors of Theorem II is written out by the worker from Definition [Canonical integral cohomological factors] (literature/blueprint/slopmaster2/src/version/sketch/01_final_weil_conjectures.tex, label def:canonical-cohomological-factors)

proof.text: *Clause (i).* By [def-weil-point-counts-zeta] (with $Y_0=X_0$), $\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})=N_n(X_0)$ and $Z(X_0,T)=\exp\bigl(\sum_{n\geq1}N_n(X_0)T^n/n\bigr)\in1+T\mathbf Q[[T]]$; this is the first displayed equality of (i), and the same definition fixes the set $|X_0|$ of closed points and $\deg(x)=[\kappa(x):\Fq]$. Theorem [thm-weil-final-rationality] applies to $X_0$ (same hypotheses, same zeta series, same closed points and degrees) and states $Z(X_0,T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]\cap\mathbf Q(T)$ and $Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}(1-T^{\deg(x)})^{-1}$. These are the second displayed equality and the membership claim of (i). The membership $Z(X_0,T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]\cap\mathbf Q(T)$ is read as in [def-weil-rational-power-series]: $Z(X_0,T)\in\mathbf Q[[T]]$ [def-weil-formal-power-series] has all coefficients in $\mathbf Z$, constant coefficient $1$, and is rational over $\mathbf Q$, i.e. $QZ(X_0,T)=P$ for polynomials $P,Q\in\mathbf Q[T]$ with $Q(0)\neq0$, its rational function being $P/Q\in\mathbf Q(T)$ [def-weil-rational-function-field]; Theorem I writes the membership with the same symbols and no other convention, so it asserts the same thing.

source.place: ## Proof, *Clause (i)*; Theorem I (literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-weil1/thm-weil-final-rationality.md) states this clause and is proved there from the propositions the paragraph cites (prop-euler-product and the rationality route)

proof.text: *Clause (ii).* By step 1, $P_i=P_i(\mathscr X)$ is the integral Frobenius factor of degree $i$ of [thm-weil-final-integrality]. That theorem states that $P_i$ is the unique polynomial in $\mathbf Z[T]$ with $P_i(0)=1$ whose coefficientwise extension $P_i^{(\ell)}=(\mathbf Z[T]\to\Ql[T])(P_i)$ equals $\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\Ql))$ for every prime $\ell\neq p$, and that $Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$. Here $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], the coefficientwise extension $(\mathbf Z[T]\to\Ql[T])(P_i)$ is that of [def-weil-coefficientwise-extension] (the same map that [thm-weil-final-integrality] and [def-weil-canonical-integral-factors] write $P_i^{(\ell)}$), and the factorization is an identity in $\mathbf Q(T)$ between the rational function of the rational power series $Z(X_0,T)$ [def-weil-rational-power-series] and $\prod_iP_i^{(-1)^{i+1}}$; equivalently, since each $P_i$ has constant coefficient $1$ and is therefore a unit of $\mathbf Q[[T]]$, it is the identity of the two sides in $\mathbf Q[[T]]$. With $F_{i,\ell}$ the restriction of $F$ to $H^i(X,\Ql)$ (step 1), these are exactly the two assertions of (ii).

source.place: ## Proof, *Clause (ii)*; Theorem II (literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-weil2/thm-weil-final-integrality.md) states this clause and is proved there from prop-integral-recovery, which the paragraph cites

proof.text: *Clause (iii).* Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$ and $0\leq i\leq2d$; put $r_i=\deg P_i$ and $P_i^\#(U)=U^{r_i}P_i(U^{-1})\in\mathbf Z[U]$. In the convention of [def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots], applied to $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}[T]$ (which has $P_i(0)=1$) with roots taken in $\overline{\mathbf Q}$, a reciprocal root of $P_i$ is an $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}^\times$ with $P_i(\alpha^{-1})=0$ and an ordinary root is a $\beta\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ with $P_i(\beta)=0$, necessarily nonzero. Since $P_i^\#(\alpha)=\alpha^{r_i}P_i(\alpha^{-1})$ for $\alpha\neq0$ and $P_i^\#(0)=[T^{r_i}]P_i\neq0$, the reciprocal roots of $P_i$ are exactly the roots of $P_i^\#$, which is the convention of Theorem [thm-weil-final-rh]; and $\beta\mapsto\beta^{-1}$ is a bijection from the ordinary roots onto the reciprocal roots, with inverse $\alpha\mapsto\alpha^{-1}$. Theorem [thm-weil-final-rh], applied to $X_0$ and the same $P_i$ (step 1), states that every reciprocal root $\alpha$ is an algebraic integer and a $q$-Weil number of weight $i$, that is $|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$ for every embedding $\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$, in the sense of [def-weil-numbers] (which fixes $\overline{\mathbf Q}$, $\mathbf Q(\alpha)$, the embeddings, algebraic integers and $q$-Weil numbers), and that $\beta=\alpha^{-1}$ satisfies $|\tau(\beta)|=q^{-i/2}$ for every embedding $\tau:\mathbf Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$. Since every ordinary root of $P_i$ is such a $\beta$, this is (iii).

source.place: ## Proof, *Clause (iii)*; Theorem III (literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-weil3/thm-weil-final-rh.md) states this clause and is proved there from prop-arithmetic-roots, which the paragraph cites; the reciprocal-root/ordinary-root correspondence is written out by the worker

proof.text:
*Clause (iv).* Put $b_i=\deg P_i$ for $0\leq i\leq2d$, the degree of the polynomial $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]; $\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql)$ is the dimension of the finite-dimensional $\Ql$-vector space $H^i(X,\Ql)$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Theorem [thm-weil-final-betti], applied to $X_0$ and the same $P_i$ (step 1), uses the same $b_i=\deg P_i$ and states: $b_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql)$ for every prime $\ell
eq p$, so that this dimension is independent of $\ell$; $b_i=b_{2d-i}$; $b_0=b_{2d}=1$; $P_0(T)=1-T$ and $P_{2d}(T)=1-q^dT$; and that the rational function $Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}\in\mathbf Q(T)$ (the one of clause (ii)) has a pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=1$ and, if $d\geq1$, a pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=q^{-d}$. A pole of order exactly $m$ at $T=a$ of the rational power series $Z(X_0,T)$ is, by [def-weil-rational-function-pole-order] (applied, as that definition says, through [def-weil-rational-power-series] to the rational function $R=\prod_iP_i^{(-1)^{i+1}}\in\mathbf Q(T)$ of $Z(X_0,T)$), the assertion that $a$ is a root of multiplicity exactly $m$ of the monic denominator $D$ of the reduced presentation $R=N/D$, $\gcd(N,D)=1$ (so $(T-a)^m\mid D$, $(T-a)^{m+1}
mid D$, and $N(a)
eq0$); Theorem IV states the two pole orders in these words, for the same rational function and with the same definition [def-weil-rational-function-pole-order], so no translation is needed. This is (iv) word for word.

source.place: ## Proof, *Clause (iv)* ('Theorem [thm-weil-final-betti] states all of these equalities for the same datum and, in addition, ... This is exactly (iv).'); the propositions the paragraph also cites (prop-integral-recovery, prop-duality-reciprocity, prop-endpoints) are the proof of Theorem IV

proof.text: *Clause (v).* With $b_i=\deg P_i$, define $D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T)$, $\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i$ and $\varepsilon=(-1)^\chi q^{-d\chi/2}\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}$ by the formulas of (v); $[T^{b_i}]P_i(T)$ is the coefficient of $T^{b_i}$ in $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$, i.e. its leading coefficient [def-weil-polynomial-ring], so $D_i$ is a nonzero integer and $D_i^{-1}$ and the product make sense in $\mathbf Q^\times$. The two displayed identities are identities in $\mathbf Q(T)$ [def-weil-rational-function-field]: $P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})$ is the polynomial $P_{2d-i}$ evaluated at $q^{-d}T^{-1}\in\mathbf Q(T)$, and $Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})$ is the substitution of $q^{-d}T^{-1}$ for $T$ in the rational function of the rational power series $Z(X_0,T)$ [def-weil-rational-power-series], the substitution being the automorphism of $\mathbf Q(T)$ of [def-weil-rational-function-field]. Theorem [thm-weil-final-functional-equation], applied to $X_0$ and the same $P_i$ (step 1), defines $D_i$, $\chi$ and $\varepsilon$ by the same three formulas, with $Z(X_0,T)$ the same point-count zeta series, and, for the same reading of $Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})$ and $P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})$ (its proof in the blueprint writes the identities 'in $\mathbf Q(T)$'), states that $d\chi$ is even, that $P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T)$ for every $0\leq i\leq2d$, and that $Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})=\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}T^\chi Z(X_0,T)$ with $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$. This is (v). The five clauses together are the statement.

source.place: ## Proof, *Clause (v)* and the closing sentence; Theorem V (literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-weil5/thm-weil-final-functional-equation.md) states this clause and is proved there from prop-duality-reciprocity, prop-functional-equation and the sign definition, which the paragraph cites; the parity of $d\chi$ (the blueprint's 'Parity of the functional-equation exponent') is part of Theorem V's statement

blueprint_notes.label: status
blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** Both Lean statements exist and both proofs are `sorry`.
`weil_conjectures` states clauses (ii), (iii) and
(v) for a smooth, proper, geometrically integral $X_0$, phrased
through the three predicates `IsWeilFactorization`,
`WeilFunctionalEquation` and `WeilRiemannHypothesis`, which are
complete definitions; `zetaSeries_rational` states the rationality
assertion of clause (i) for an arbitrary scheme of finite type over
$\Fq$.

split_report.summary: Statement unchanged (GOAL.md states it word for word). Checked the six imported steps against the master md and the identical slopmaster2 LaTeX proof (01_final_weil_conjectures.tex, thm:weil-final, lines 3557-3760): each paragraph only names the propositions behind one clause and says the clause follows, so none was a proof of the clause from the propositions. The four title-only references the import could not resolve are definitions and a proposition that exist only in the slopmaster2 LaTeX sketch: 'Smooth-proper datum' and 'Canonical integral cohomological factors' are the nodes def-weil-smooth-proper-datum and def-weil-canonical-integral-factors (the latter takes its tuple from prop-integral-recovery, the master counterpart of prop:integral-factor-existence, and now cites the existing leaves def-weil-coefficientwise-extension and def-weil-polynomial-ring instead of redefining P^(l)); 'Frobenius characteristic factors' (LaTeX lines 2899-2917) is the determinant family P_{i,l} already inside def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family; 'Euler characteristic' is chi inside def-weil-determinant-constants; 'Parity of the functional-equation exponent' is the assertion 'd chi is even' of thm-weil-final-functional-equation. The proof is the assembly the master frontmatter declares: step 1 identifies the datum and, by the uniqueness in thm-weil-final-integrality, the canonical factors with the integral Frobenius factors that Theorems I-V are stated for; steps 2-6 show that clauses (i)-(v) are, for these objects, exactly the statements of thm-weil-final-rationality, -integrality, -rh, -betti and -functional-equation, compared statement against statement (clause (iii) needs the elementary reciprocal-root/ordinary-root correspondence, written out; def-weil-ordinary-reciprocal-roots is stated for polynomials over Q_l with roots in Q_l-bar, and clause (iii) applies the same words to P_i over Q-bar, so the step spells the convention out and matches it with the roots of P_i^# used by Theorem III). The propositions the text cites (prop-euler-product, prop-integral-recovery, prop-arithmetic-roots, prop-duality-reciprocity, prop-endpoints, prop-functional-equation) and the two sign/constant definitions are each used by the theorem whose clause they prove (checked in those theorems' proof_deps) and remain reached through it; they are no longer direct dependencies of the target. Statement dependencies now name every notion the statement uses. Three standard notions had no node (def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction, prop-integral-recovery and thm-weil-final-betti use them undefined). Two are new Mathlib leaves created for this item: def-weil-rational-function-field (K(T) with reduced presentation, value at a point and substitution of a transcendental element, needed for T -> q^{-d}T^{-1} in clause (v); RatFunc) and def-weil-rational-power-series (f in K[[T]] with Qf=P, Q(0)!=0, its rational function P/Q, and the reading of '1+TZ[[T]] cap Q(T)' and of assertions about Z 'in Q(T)'; one line over PowerSeries/RatFunc/LaurentSeries, no named Mathlib predicate). The third, the pole of order exactly m, is taken from def-weil-rational-function-order-at-point, created meanwhile (uncommitted) by the worker on thm-weil-final-betti: it defines ord_c on K(T) in lowest terms and 'pole of order exactly m' as ord_c = -m, with the same Mathlib match (Polynomial.rootMultiplicity on RatFunc.num/denom); the node def-weil-rational-function-pole-order that the previous worker's citation announced was therefore not delivered (a draft of it, written before that node appeared, was withdrawn before any commit). That node also defines K(T) and lowest terms in its preamble, which overlaps the first paragraph of def-weil-rational-function-field; the lead may make it cite def-weil-rational-function-field instead. The existing leaves def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-coefficientwise-extension and def-weil-vector-space-dimension are now cited for Z[T], deg, [T^b]P, the map Z[T]->Q_l[T] and dim_{Q_l}, in the statement and in the steps that use them. Lean (slopmaster2 and master identical, WeilConjectures/Statement.lean, both declarations sorry): weil_conjectures (lines 86-98) takes a finite field k (q = Nat.card k), d : N and f : X -> Spec k with [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [IsProper f] [GeometricallyIntegral f] -- geometrically integral where the node says geometrically connected -- and states the existence of P : Fin (2d+1) -> Z[T] with IsWeilFactorization q d f.zetaSeries P (P_i(0)=1 for all i, P_0 = 1-T, P_{2d} = 1-q^d T, and zetaSeries * prod_{i even} P_i = prod_{i odd} P_i in Q[[T]]), WeilFunctionalEquation q d P (for every i, the multiset of complex roots of P_{2d-i} is the image of that of P_i under z -> 1/(q^d z)) and WeilRiemannHypothesis q d P (every complex root z of P_i has |z| = q^{-i/2}) (Comparator/Weil/Definitions.lean). So it states: the factorization of clause (ii) as an existence statement, without the uniqueness of the P_i and without their cohomological characterization P_i^(l) = det(1-TF | H^i(X,Q_l)); the endpoint factors P_0, P_{2d} of clause (iv), without b_i = dim H^i, b_i = b_{2d-i} and the pole orders; the ordinary-root form |tau(beta)| = q^{-i/2} of clause (iii) (algebraic integrality and the reciprocal-root form follow from P_i in Z[T], P_i(0)=1); and the root-multiset form of the degreewise reciprocity of clause (v), which implies the Laurent identity P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1}) = (-1)^{b_i} T^{-b_i} D_i^{-1} P_i(T) and the functional equation for Z with some sign, but does not state the parity of d chi, the formula for epsilon, or the displayed functional equation itself. zetaSeries_rational (lines 77-84) states, for any f locally of finite type and quasi-compact over a finite field, the existence of P, Q in Z[T] with Q(0)=1 and zetaSeries * Q = P in Q[[T]]: the rationality of clause (i) (with an integral presentation, which gives the membership in 1+TZ[[T]] cap Q(T)), without the Euler product; the exp description of clause (i) is the Lean definition of zetaSeries (pointCount n = #X(F_{q^n}) via the splitting field of X^{q^n}-X). No Lean declaration states the Euler product, the uniqueness or cohomological meaning of the P_i, or the Betti and pole assertions of clause (iv). Third pass (interrupted twice before): step 5 cited a node def-weil-rational-function-order-at-point that was never created; the existing leaf def-weil-rational-function-pole-order (created for this item, Mathlib match Polynomial.rootMultiplicity on RatFunc.denom, and already used by thm-weil-final-betti) defines exactly the notion clause (iv) uses, 'pole of order exactly m at T=a' of a rational function and of a rational power series, so step 5, stmt_deps and proof_deps now cite it and step 5 reads the pole order as the multiplicity of a as a root of the reduced denominator, as that leaf does; no new node was needed. Rechecked: statement unchanged and equal to GOAL.md; every cited id exists and is unmerged; each step names what it uses and none is elementary; proof_deps is the union of the uses; check_dag.py and review_split.py report nothing on this node.
